facts.value: gold-answer bits-per-byte is the small-scale capability proxy the literature converges on, and it is NOT corpus BPB. Definition (OLMo 3 arXiv 2512.13961 §3.3.2): negative log-likelihood of the gold answer divided by the number of UTF-8 bytes in the answer string, over tasks 'that have gold labels or human-written answers'. Its stated motivation is our exact problem -- small-compute models 'exhibit random-chance performance on math, code, and multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) tasks'. Gold strings in AI2's olmes implementation (https://github.com/allenai/olmes): HumanEval canonical_solution (codex_humaneval.py:149), MBPP code field (codex_mbpp.py:213, with perplexity_leading_space=False under the bpb variant), Minerva MATH human-written solution (minerva_math.py:198). The contrast that matters: held-out CORPUS perplexity as a downstream proxy measures .332/.380/.354 pairwise accuracy across 50 1B variants (Sun et al. arXiv 2504.12491 Table 1), BELOW the 0.500 random baseline, and Gadre names code the worst extrapolation domain. Our domain_loss is corpus-level and remains a data-pricing instrument, not a capability proxy. Normalise per UTF-8 byte, not per character: byte normalisation is tokenizer-invariant, which matters more for a zh-optimised 32K vocab than for the English work this comes from.
facts.source: OLMo 3 arXiv 2512.13961 §3.3.2; AI2 olmes (upstream, not this repo) oe_eval/configs/task_suites.py:931-1005 (https://github.com/allenai/olmes/blob/main/oe_eval/configs/task_suites.py#L931-L1005); Sun et al. arXiv 2504.12491 Table 1; DataDecide arXiv 2504.11393 §3.3-3.4

facts.value: admission rule for whether a task belongs in the decision loop at all, adopted 2026-08-31: a task qualifies only if at least one 0.154B model trained on as many as 99B tokens reaches 10 percentage points above chance (Gadre et al. §3.4). 154M params is our scale, which is why this rule is quotable here rather than extrapolated. Of 46 tasks, 17 qualified; MMLU, ARC-Challenge, MathQA and OpenBookQA were excluded, MMLU named as 'close to random chance'. Corollary that cost us a wrong inference: DataDecide's SNR ranks ARC-Challenge at 4.27, above PIQA, while its absolute headroom at 150M is 1.3pt. High power to separate DATA RECIPES is not a readable capability signal, and only the latter admits a task to the profile.

The pair below is a STEP-SAVE vs a RUN-END SAVE, which are different code paths: the run-end save happens after the training loop, carries no optimizer state and records step: None. A post-loop save could differ SYSTEMATICALLY from a mid-training snapshot, not just randomly, so the 2.9 pt may be a step-save/run-end-save OFFSET with jitter on top rather than jitter. The measurement is one difference correctly measured and possibly wrongly named.

Two checkpoints from the SAME run at the same seed and config, scored on the same stage-1 heads under the milestone profile: step16000 and the run-end save (ckpt_pretrain_15b_s1.pt, no step suffix). Per-role domain loss moves 0.005-0.027 nat. C-Eval moves 22.5 -> 25.4, i.e. 2.9 pt. code_500 degeneration moves 0.522 -> 0.628, i.e. 10.6 pt. So at fixed seed a generative or MC metric's checkpoint-to-checkpoint jitter is far larger than its seed-to-seed variance, while per-role domain loss is stable to within a fifth of its own threshold.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. Loss is stable and the generative metrics are not, over a gap small enough that no real capability change is plausible. Anything read off ceval or a degeneration rate between two nearby checkpoints is mostly which checkpoint you took.

WHAT IT IMPLIES FOR THE CEVAL GATE, recorded here as an observation and referred to 44 as a prereg amendment rather than applied: the pre-registered threshold is 5.9 pt = 4.65 x seed SD 1.27 (be.panel_expressive_seed_variance). Adjacent-checkpoint jitter of 2.9 pt is 2.3x that seed SD, so the threshold rests on the smaller of two independent noise terms. No verdict recorded on 2026-08-31/09-01 changes: every ceval reading was floor, and a larger threshold only makes floor more certain -- including the 25.4, which read as the first move out of the 22-23 band and sits inside this jitter. The live consequence is forward-looking: a future ceval move between roughly 6 and 13 pt would be unsafe to call on the 5.9 figure. The 5.9 stays the record of what was pre-registered.

facts.claim: whether generate_batch's default repetition-stop biases every degeneration and repetition number this repo has published
facts.value: YES, and the bias is roughly 1.8x DOWNWARD. train.generate_batch defaults rep_stop=True (train.py:1176), which halts decoding when a whitespace 8-gram repeats 3x -- which is the definition of the degenerate-repetition metric itself. So the generation is cut at the moment it satisfies the predicate, and any rate computed over the stored tail is a rate over a truncated prefix. MEASURED A/B on ckpt_pretrain_30b_s2.pt.step24000, 48 code-holdout prompts, greedy, max_new 512, identical prompts and seed: rep_stop=True gives 19/48 = 39.6% degenerate at mean 208 tokens; rep_stop=False gives 35/48 = 72.9% at mean 512 tokens. The stop does not merely shorten the text, it removes generations from the numerator: a generation that would have looped for another 300 tokens is stopped early and, on the truncated tail, no longer trips the 3x threshold. SCOPE OF THE CONTAMINATION: every degeneration/repetition figure produced through this helper is a lower bound, not a measurement -- this includes be.degeneration_rate's code base 3-shot 6.6%, base 0-shot 25.4%, SFT v2 greedy 55.8% and SFT v2 t=0.8 17.0%, and any code-500/math-500 degeneration rate quoted from an eval that used the default. The 1.8x factor is measured on ONE checkpoint at ONE max_new and must not be applied as a correction multiplier to those figures; it establishes direction and rough size, not a conversion. CAPABILITY numbers (pass@1, accuracy) are NOT affected: a truncated degenerate generation was going to score 0 either way. The affected class is exactly the format/degeneration family. WHAT TO DO: any probe measuring repetition must pass rep_stop=False and say so in its artifact; rep_stop=True remains correct for capability evals, where it saves compute on generations that are already lost.
facts.source: e1, A/B on the pod GPU7; probes/t69_copy_rate.py@be8e94a and probes/t67_self_repeat.py@d217bad both pass rep_stop=False
facts.uncertainty: One checkpoint, one max_new, 48 prompts; the ratio is direction-and-size, not a conversion factor. At a smaller max_new the two arms converge, because the stop has less room to act -- so the bias is largest exactly where generations are longest.
facts.boundary: Found by READING generate_batch's signature while writing a probe, not by running anything -- the argument is a default, it is documented in the docstring, and it had been in every call site for months. A guard that is correct for its original purpose becomes a confound the moment the thing it guards against becomes the thing under test.

facts.claim: why the 22B checkpoint's generations look like verbatim repetition, and what that implies for its capability zeros
facts.value: THE MODEL DOES NOT COPY ITS CONTEXT -- IT REPEATS ITSELF, AND ONLY UNDER GREEDY DECODING. Two behaviours read identically in a bug report and have different causes and different fixes: reproducing the PROMPT (context-copying) and reproducing ITS OWN OUTPUT (self-repetition). Measured on ckpt_pretrain_30b_s2.pt.step24000, 62 code-holdout prompts, 8-gram in TOKENS, rep_stop=False, one prompt set across all arms. COPY-FROM-CONTEXT (t62): greedy median 0.000 (p90 0.4615), sampled t=0.8 median 0.000 (p90 0.0435), 3-shot greedy median 0.4308 (p90 0.8611). Against the pre-registered <=0.30 falsification line, greedy 0.000 REFUTES the copy hypothesis outright; the few-shot arm copies MORE, which is in-context pattern-matching rather than copying and is the opposite of the predicted direction. SELF-REPETITION (t63, max_new 256): greedy median 0.747, p90 0.9558, 74.2% of generations at >=0.5, median longest repeated run 175 tokens; sampled t=0.8 median 0.0884, p90 0.5462, 11.3% at >=0.5, median run 9. The pathology is a property of GREEDY DECODING on this checkpoint, not of the weights. IT IS A MIXTURE, NOT A UNIFORM STATE, and this is the part that changes a decision: 74% of greedy generations loop, and the remaining 26% are fluent, on-topic, WRONG Chinese technical prose with no looping at all. Read from the dump rather than inferred from the statistic. A model producing fluent on-topic prose a quarter of the time is not a broken model -- it is an untuned base model with a decoding pathology on top. CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY CAPABILITY ZERO AT THIS CHECKPOINT: code_500 0.0 and similar are scored partly because greedy decoding puts three quarters of generations into a loop, not only because the model knows nothing. The two causes are not separated by any measurement we currently have, and 'capability zero' must not be read as 'learned nothing' until they are. DOMAIN CHECK (e1, same day, before the finding hardened): the code-only result was n=62 from ONE domain and the looping text was Chinese prose about code, so 'the model loops' was one repo-wide belief away from resting on a single prompt set. Re-ran on math_test_500, 64 prompts, same checkpoint and settings: greedy median 0.7711 (p90 0.9116), 79.7% at >=0.5, median run 172; sampled t=0.8 median 0.0060 (p90 0.2000), 3.2% at >=0.5, median run 2. The pathology is NOT code-specific -- math greedy is marginally worse (0.771 vs 0.747) and math sampled is markedly cleaner (0.006 vs 0.088). Two domains, same shape, same direction, and the greedy-vs-sampled gap is if anything wider on math.

CODE-500: gold token in the model's top-1 at a median 72.7% of positions (p10 0.592, p90 0.796), top-10 90.7%, top-100 95.9%, median gold length 36 tokens. MATH-500: top-1 69.3% (p10 0.614, p90 0.758), top-10 90.6%, top-100 97.8%, median gold length 184.5 tokens. Ties barely matter -- the pessimistic rank (ties counted against the gold) is 0.7209 and 0.6889, within 0.005 of the optimistic one -- so the distribution is genuinely peaked and not flat. AGAINST THE PRE-REGISTERED TABLE: top-1 >= 0.50 puts both sets in the decoding band and well clear of the <= 0.15 knowledge band. WHAT THIS MEANS PRACTICALLY: the per-token distribution is close to correct and the SEQUENCE is not, which is the signature of error compounding -- at 72.7% per-token top-1 accuracy, a 36-token gold has probability 0.727^36 ~ 1e-5 of being produced greedily even if every position were independent. facts.claim: how much seed evidence it takes to know the seed noise, measured on two independent families
facts.value: TWO INDEPENDENT FOUR-SEED FAMILIES DISAGREE ABOUT THE NOISE BY A FACTOR OF TWO. Found free in runs/experiments.jsonl + runs/score_matrix.jsonl -- no new compute -- while sizing a seed arm for the FoNE A/B. Both families are mix_scale_0.2b, same config, `--seed N` the only difference, mean domain loss over scored domains. p02: seeds 0-3 give 3.7588 / 3.8085 / 3.7433 / 3.7009, spread 0.1076, sd 0.0444. p02_fp32m: 3.8693 / 3.8379 / 3.8874 / 3.8403, spread 0.0495, sd 0.0239. THE CONSEQUENCE IS GENERAL AND OUTLIVES FoNE: four seeds is more than anyone here normally spends on a noise estimate, and a single four-seed family would have mis-stated the noise by 2x IN AN UNKNOWN DIRECTION. Only having two families reveals it; with one, the number looks like a measurement. So a noise bound from a single family is a point estimate with an uncharacterised error, and any A/B threshold set as a multiple of it inherits that error. WHICH TO USE: the LARGER family. Understating noise ships a null as a finding, which is the more expensive error in both directions -- it costs the work built on the false positive plus the credibility of the next real one.
